info.title: Kofra API
info.summary: Manage a Kofra storage workspace programmatically.
info.description:
The Kofra API manages a storage workspace: buckets, S3 access keys, usage,
the account's state and its event feed. Object data is never sent to this
API; read and write objects through the S3 endpoint with any S3 tool, or
with a presigned URL from `POST /v1/objects/presign`.

**Status: draft.** This contract is published ahead of the service. The
mock server in the repository answers every operation with the examples
below.

Conventions:

- Authentication: `Authorization: Bearer <API token>`. A token belongs to
  exactly one workspace, so paths carry no workspace ID.
- Errors: RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`, a
  one-sentence `hint` and a `docs_url`. See the error catalogue.
- Lists: cursor pagination with `limit` (1 to 200, default 50) and
  `cursor`; the body has `data` and `next_cursor` (`null` at the end), and
  a `Link: <...>; rel="next"` header repeats it.
- Writes: `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` accept `Idempotency-Key`, kept 24
  hours and bound to the method, path, query and body of its first
  request. Destructive operations accept `dry_run=true`.
- Every response carries `Kofra-Request-Id`, `RateLimit` and
  `RateLimit-Policy`; `429` and `503` also carry `Retry-After`, and `401`
  carries `WWW-Authenticate`.
- Unknown request fields and undeclared or repeated query parameters are
  refused (`unknown_field`, `validation_failed`). Clients must ignore
  unknown response fields, and treat an unknown enum value in a response
  as "other": new fields and new enum values are added within `/v1`.
- Timestamps are RFC 3339 UTC. Sizes are integers in bytes, in fields that
  end in `_bytes`.

delete.description:
Starts a deletion of the whole workspace. The deletion is not scheduled
until a signed-in Owner confirms it in the console: the answer carries
the `confirm_url` to open. Until it is confirmed, nothing changes.

After confirmation every bucket, object and key stops being reachable,
and the data is cryptographically erased at `erase_at`. Until then the
deletion can be cancelled with `POST /v1/account/deletion/cancel`.

Scopes: `account:delete`.

200.description: Dry run. What the deletion would do; nothing was changed.

value.summary: Deletes the workspace: 3 buckets, 18,342 objects, 412 GiB and 4 access keys stop being reachable once confirmed.

202.description: The deletion request was created and waits for confirmation in the console.

long as `erase_at` has not passed. The account, its buckets and its keys
work again at once.

post.description:
Creates an S3 access key pair with access to the listed buckets. The
secret is in this response only; store it at once. A replay of the same
request with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the key with
`secret_access_key: null`: revoke that key and create a new one if the
secret was lost.

Whoever holds a key with access to a bucket can read its objects, so
`keys:write` is treated as data access. The grants cannot exceed the
caller's own access: a grant on a bucket, or an access level, that the
caller's role does not allow is refused with `role_forbidden`.

Through the MCP tool `keys_create`, the secret is not in the tool
result: the result links to a console page that shows it once.

Scopes: `keys:write`.

201.description: The key was created. The secret is shown once.

patch.description:
Renames a key, or adds or widens its grants. A grant is never narrowed
(`read_write` to `read`) or removed: create a new key with the narrower
access and revoke this one. Grants not listed are left as they are.

Scopes: `keys:write`.

200.description: The key as it is now.

bearerAuth.description:
An API token from the console, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
Tokens carry scopes; each operation names the scopes it needs.
Scopes: `account:read`, `account:delete`, `buckets:read`,
`buckets:write`, `buckets:delete`, `keys:read`, `keys:write`,
`usage:read`, `events:read`, `objects:read`. A token's effective
permission is its scopes limited by its member's workspace role.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The `next_cursor` from the previous page. Omit for the first page.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Makes a retry safe: the same key and the same request within 24 hours return the first answer. The key is bound to the method, the path, the query and the body of its first request: `dry_run=true` and a request without it (or with `dry_run=false`, which is the same request) are different requests and need different keys. 1 to 255 printable ASCII characters; a UUID is a good choice.

DryRun.name: dry_run
DryRun.description: When `true`, answer `200` with the plan of what would change, and change nothing.

BucketName.description: 3 to 63 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens; starts and ends with a letter or digit.

Cursor.description: An opaque position in a list. Pass it back unchanged.

state.description:
`active`: normal service. `suspended`: see `suspension`. `deleting`:
a confirmed deletion is in progress; see `deletion`.

access.description: What S3 requests can do now. `read_only` allows reads, lists and deletes.

s3_endpoint.description: The S3 endpoint for this workspace's buckets.

storage_bytes.description: Most bytes the workspace may store. `null` means no fixed limit.

upload_24h_bytes.description: Most bytes that may be uploaded in any 24 hours. `null` means no fixed limit.

download_allowance_bytes.description: Bytes that may be downloaded per billing period. `null` means no fixed allowance.

active_keys.description: Most active S3 access keys at once.

confirm_url.description: Console page where a signed-in Owner confirms. `null` once confirmed.

erase_at.description: When the data is cryptographically erased. `null` until confirmed.

Plan.description: The answer to `dry_run=true`. Nothing was changed.

summary.description: One plain sentence describing the effect.

reversible.description: Whether the change could be undone after it is made.

PlanTotals.description: What the planned change reaches, in total.

Grant.description: One bucket an access key can reach, and how.

access.description: `read`: list and read objects. `read_write`: also write and delete objects.

GrantInput.description: A grant in a request. Each bucket at most once per request; a bucket listed twice is refused with `validation_failed`.

access.description: `read`: list and read objects. `read_write`: also write and delete objects.

name.description: A label for people; not used for access.

AccessKeyCreated.description: An access key with its secret. The secret appears in this response only.

secret_access_key.description: The S3 secret access key. `null` when this is a replay of an earlier request.

grants.description: The buckets the key can reach. Each bucket at most once.

AccessKeyUpdate.description: At least one of `name` and `grants`. An empty `grants` list is refused; leave `grants` out to keep the grants as they are.

grants.description: Grants to add or widen. Grants not listed are kept. Each bucket at most once. A key holds at most 32 grants.

KeyName.description: A label for people; not used for access.

Grants.description: 1 to 32 grants, each bucket at most once; a bucket listed twice is refused with `validation_failed`.

OverLimit.description: Set while stored bytes are above the storage limit.

deadline_at.description: When writes stop unless usage is reduced or the limit raised. `null` if no deadline applies.

Downloads.description: Downloads in the current billing period.

OpenUploads.description: Multipart uploads started and not yet completed or aborted.

requests_approx.description: Approximate number of S3 requests that day.

data.description: Event-specific fields. Never holds a secret.

next_cursor.description: The position to continue from. Never `null` for the feed.

method.description: Only downloads are offered for now.

PresignLifetime.description: How long the URL stays valid, in seconds, 1 to 900 (15 minutes). Default 900.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details with Kofra's fields. Only `code` is stable.

type.description: A page describing this error code.

code.description: Stable machine name; see the error catalogue. New codes may be added within `/v1`.

hint.description: What to do next, in one sentence.

docs_url.description: The Markdown version of the error page.

request_id.description: Same as the `Kofra-Request-Id` header. Quote it to support.

retryable.description: Whether the same request may succeed if repeated (after `Retry-After`, when given).

errors.description: Per-field problems, for `validation_failed`, `unknown_field` and similar codes.

pointer.description: JSON pointer to the field (RFC 6901), or `#query/<name>`, `#path/<name>` or `#header/<name>` for parameters.

KofraRequestId.description: Unique ID of this request. The same ID is in the error body and the audit log; quote it to support.

RateLimit.description: Remaining allowance of the policy that applies (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers).

RateLimitPolicy.description: The rate-limit policies that apply to this credential (draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers).

WWWAuthenticate.description: The authentication challenge (RFC 6750): `Bearer realm="kofra"`, with `error="invalid_token"` when a token was sent but is not usable.

Link.description: The next page, as `<url>; rel="next"`, while more follow.
